items.title: Javon Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Bucky Pizzarelli; the mention comes solely from the interviewer stating 'I knew Bucky Pizzarelli pretty well'.

ctx.x: Several. Jimmy Heath was a very close friend and mentor. Jimmy passed. Jimmy Cobb was a very close friend and mentor. He just passed recently. McCoy Tyner was someone I had been working with over the last two, three years, he passed. Wallace Roney, who was a bandmate and good friend and someone I learned an immense amount from, he passed. Musicians in Denver that I knew have passed, a couple, and obviously the Marsalis family, Delfeayo was someone I went to college with, the passing of his father, you feel…

Yeah somehow I had to correct myself — I knew Bucky Pizzarelli pretty well and he had been to Hamilton many times, and when he passed away I just felt like that’s not fair somehow, that this took him down even though he was in poor health. And I had to stop myself and say it’s not fair for anybody that’s losing — it’s not just musicians it’s across the board as you had said.

Right. I forgot to mention Lee Konitz, a person I’m very fond of and a mentor as well. There’s been so many, you’re right, in some ways it doesn’t seem fair, but at the same time I think that it might not be wise for me to question so much as opposed to appreciating that time and that person and that spirit, and allow that to be something that I can surround myself and put my arms around that as opposed to why this person and why not this person, and why this person. Because everyone is going through something of…
